text:
dina: Opening PRD intake — we need to align on throughput SLO vs cost for tenant burst scenarios. Problem: several customers hit ~2x baseline QPS during marketing spikes and we don't have a clear, low-risk fallback that preserves latency and cost.

ben: quick q — are we targeting hosted API only or Dedicated + Private?

dina: primarily Dedicated (customers on reserved pools), but solution should be portable to hosted policies. Non-goal: re-architecting autoscaler.

alexa: goals I'd expect: (1) clear acceptance criteria for "burst handled" (p99 < X ms, error rate < Y%), (2) measurable unit-cost delta <= Z%, (3) rollback triggers defined.

chris: +1 to that. For rollout: suggest canary (5 tenants, mixed sizes) -> 25% traffic -> 100%. Track: p50/p95/p99 latency, token-cost per request, queue length, degraded-response-rate.

ben: edge cases: noisy neighbor where multiple tenants burst simultaneously, TTLs for prefix cache invalidation, and per-tenant config abuse (someone sets infinite burst). We need caps and a safety limiter.

alexa: thinking of three levers: per-tenant burst budget, priority routing (route to cheaper model variant when under pressure), and graceful degradation (trim context, shorter responses).

dina: sketch of acceptance criteria (proposal):
- Latency: p99 <= 650ms for burst tier requests (measured at gateway)
- Availability: successful responses >= 99.5% during 10m sustained 2x baseline bursts
- Cost: unit-cost increase <= 30% vs baseline over a burst window
- Quality: automated evals maintain >= 95% of baseline QA score for sampled prompts

ben: those numbers look reasonable as starting point. Need to define how QA score is computed and sample size. Also how long is the evaluation window?

dina: suggest 1k sampled prompts across tenants over burst window; use existing eval harness.

chris: rollout playbook idea:
1) feature flag that enables per-tenant burst caps + routing policy
2) metric dashboards + alert if cost-per-token rises > 20% or p99 > 700ms
3) canary on 5 tenants for 48hrs, compare baseline metrics
4) expand traffic to 25% for 24hrs, then GA if stable

alexa: config snippet for caps (example):
```
tenant_burst_budget: 100_000_tokens_per_day
burst_window: 10m
fallback_model: gpt-small-q4
priority: standard | reduced
```

prod-bot: PRD template link: https://redwood.company/prd-template — please fill problem, goals, non-goals, acceptance criteria before EOD Fri.

dina: next steps: ben & alexa draft the acceptance criteria + experiment plan by Tues, chris to prepare dashboards, I'll sync with SEs to pick canary tenants. If nobody objects I'll move to RFC stage by Wed. :thumbsup:

ben: noted, will start drafting.

alexa: I'll add edge cases and abuser mitigation (per-tenant token throttles + alerts).

chris: will add dashboard mocks and alert thresholds.

dina: cool — thanks everyone. If you have conflicting constraints (regulatory, privacy) flag in the doc so we can scope non-goals.

ben: one more ask — include cost attribution per-tenant broken down by model variant and routing. Important for sales discussions.

dina: good call, adding to metrics.
